issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (UML and textual instruction), but both the provided template and the reference solution use the method name singFarmSong(). This name mismatch between the specification and the codebase can confuse students about which method to implement and where to put the song logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all materials. Either (a) update the problem statement to instruct students to implement singFarmSong() (matching the template and solution), or (b) change the template and solution to provide/implement printFarmSong() and ensure the UML, instructions, and code all use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() in Farm.java, but both the template and the solution define and use a method named singFarmSong() for the same functionality (playing/printing the farm song). This naming mismatch (printFarmSong vs singFarmSong) can confuse students about which method to implement and which method will be used by the provided code (e.g., Main) or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either (a) rename singFarmSong() in the template and solution to printFarmSong(), and update all references (Main, UML, comments), or (b) update the problem statement and UML to instruct implementing singFarmSong() instead of printFarmSong(). Ensure all examples and the Main class use the same method name.
